benchmark_kind: owner-blind pooling versus uniform padding on a realistic MetaQA federation
scope_warning: Degree figures and per-owner volumes are measured from the raw MetaQA graph. The cost comparison is analytic, using coefficients measured elsewhere in this directory; no MPC was run at this scale. The federation split is constructed, not given -- see below.
why_this_exists: metaqa_federated_split_reality_check.json found the bundled two-party split has a volume skew of 1.003, which removes the motivation for hiding per-owner volume. That split is a random 50/50 partition of edges: 61% of sources appear in BOTH parties with the same relations. It is a property of how this project partitioned MetaQA, not a property of MetaQA, and it is the least realistic federation available.

split_used.rule: by relation type, three owners -- institutions holding different record types
split_used.note: Other realistic splits give comparable skew: by subject entity 1.83x over four owners, one-large-archive 2.02x. A random edge split gives 1.01x.

padding_overhead.reading: Uniform padding inflates every owner's pool to the largest, adding 31.4% to the page-pool scan on EVERY query.

headline: At the MEASURED max (source,relation) degree of 2,089, pooling repays its one-time cost after 1.6 queries. Even at the old assumed page_size of 16 it repays after 214. Across the whole plausible range pooling beats padding for any realistic epoch, and it is strictly more private: padding publishes max B_i, pooling publishes only the federation total.
the_caveat_that_matters: The favourable end of this range is driven by page_size being forced to 2,089, which is itself a consequence of the relation-narrowing premise failing on MetaQA. Pooling looks best precisely where the paged layout looks worst. Reporting the break-even without page_size alongside it would be misleading.
what_this_does_not_show: Any executed run; the comparison is analytic from measured coefficients.
That the relation-type split is the right federation model for MetaQA; it is defensible but constructed.
Any fix for the relation-narrowing failure, which is independent and unresolved.
